title: Regional temperature profiles (rectal/sternal/nasal) during stop-flow perfusion with hemofiltration
summary:
During a special form of chemotherapy called stop-flow perfusion, the blood flow in a specific body region is temporarily blocked to allow the medication to work more effectively. This procedure can lead to a significant drop in body temperature.

As part of an internal quality check, the medical team began monitoring patient temperatures more closely. Early results showed that many patients cooled down substantially during the procedure – in some cases even to 32 °C.

As a result, formal approval was obtained to collect temperature data systematically in 50 patients. However, after 40 patients, the study was stopped early and a medical warming device was purchased. Once the warming system was available, continuing treatment without it was no longer considered safe.

In the next phase, 40 more patients will undergo the same procedure with continuous warming. The goal is to compare both groups to better understand temperature changes during treatment and to improve patient safety through more effective warming measures.

There is no additional burden for patients: the care process remains the same, and only one extra temperature sensor is used during surgery.
conditions: Intraoperative hypothermia during stop-flow perfusion with hemofiltration; analysis of regional temperature profiles to guide development of thermal protection strategies.

interventions.name: Temperature measurement during stop-flow chemotherapy without concomitant heat application (current standard treatment protocol.
Temperature monitoring during stop-flow chemotherapy with continuous air-flow heat application throughout the entire intraoperative treatment phase.

criteria:

stop-flow perfusion chemotherapy / regional chemotherapy
Exclusion criteria:
